{{Short description|National Basketball Association honor}}

{{Use mdy dates|date=May 2013}}
{{NBA Awards}}
[[File:LeBron James (51959977144) (cropped2).jpg|thumb|upright|[[LeBron James]] has been selected to the All-NBA team a record 21 times, including a record 13 times as a member of the All-NBA first team.]]
The '''All-NBA Team''' is an annual [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) honor bestowed on the best players in the league following every NBA season. The voting is conducted by a global panel of sportswriters and broadcasters.{{efn|The voting panel was from the United States and Canada before expanding in 2017.<ref name=nba_05262016/><ref>{{cite press release|title=Russell Westbrook, James Harden, LeBron James lead 2016-17 All-NBA first team|date=May 18, 2017|publisher=NBA|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2017/05/18/all-nba-teams-2017-release|access-date=September 24, 2020|archive-date=September 29, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929180018/https://www.nba.com/article/2017/05/18/all-nba-teams-2017-release|url-status=live}}</ref>}} The team has been selected in every season of the league's existence, dating back to its inaugural season in [[1946–47 BAA season|1946]].<ref name="all-nba_b">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/history/awards_allnba.html|title=All-NBA Teams|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|work=NBA.com|access-date=August 7, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080917173421/http://www.nba.com/history/awards_allnba.html|archive-date=September 17, 2008}}</ref> The All-NBA Team originally had two teams, but since [[1987–88 NBA season|1988]] it is composed of three five-man lineups—a first, second, and third team.

From [[1955–56 NBA season|1956]] through [[2022–23 NBA season|2023]],<ref>{{cite news|first=Kevin|last=O'Connor|title=Picking the 2019 NBA All-Star Teams|date=January 21, 2019|work=The Ringer|url=https://www.theringer.com/nba/2019/1/21/18191002/picking-2019-nba-all-star-teams|access-date=September 27, 2020|archive-date=November 7, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201107234122/https://www.theringer.com/nba/2019/1/21/18191002/picking-2019-nba-all-star-teams|url-status=live}}</ref> voters selected two [[Guard (basketball)|guards]], two [[Forward (basketball)|forwards]], and one [[Center (basketball)|center]] for each team.<ref name=nba_05262016>{{cite press release|title=Warriors' Stephen Curry and Cavaliers' LeBron James headline 2015-16 All-NBA First Team|date=May 26, 2016|publisher=NBA|url=https://pr.nba.com/2015-16-all-nba-teams/|access-date=September 21, 2020|archive-date=October 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022063002/https://pr.nba.com/2015-16-all-nba-teams/|url-status=live}}</ref> This contrasts with the voting for [[Starting lineup|starters]] of the [[NBA All-Star Game]], which has chosen two [[backcourt (basketball)|backcourt]] and three [[frontcourt]] players since [[2013 NBA All-Star Game|2013]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Aschburner|title=Commissioner Adam Silver discusses league's 'positionless basketball' at Finals press conference|date=June 3, 2022|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-commissioner-adam-silver-discusses-leagues-positionless-basketball-at-annual-finals-press-conference|access-date=August 9, 2022|archive-date=August 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809095414/https://www.nba.com/news/nba-commissioner-adam-silver-discusses-leagues-positionless-basketball-at-annual-finals-press-conference|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Casciaro|title=The All-NBA selection process needs to evolve with the times|work=TheScore|date=April 5, 2022 |url=https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/2331362/amp|access-date=August 9, 2022}}</ref> The NBA's sister league, the [[Women's National Basketball Association]] (WNBA), announced late in its [[2022 WNBA season|2022 season]] that it was changing the composition of its [[All-WNBA Team]]s from the All-NBA format to a "positionless" format in which members are selected without regard to position.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.wnba.com/news/wnba-announces-new-process-for-selecting-all-wnba-teams-and-unveils-end-of-season-awards-schedule/ |title=WNBA Announces New Process for Selecting All-WNBA Teams and Unveils End-of-Season Awards Schedule |publisher=WNBA |date=August 5, 2022 |access-date=August 7, 2022 |archive-date=August 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807011504/https://www.wnba.com/news/wnba-announces-new-process-for-selecting-all-wnba-teams-and-unveils-end-of-season-awards-schedule/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Mike D. II|last=Sykes|title=The WNBA's new All-WNBA voting system is perfect and the NBA should take notes|date=August 5, 2022|work=USA Today|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2022/08/all-wnba-voting-process-perfect-nba|access-date=August 9, 2022|archive-date=August 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809095527/https://ftw.usatoday.com/2022/08/all-wnba-voting-process-perfect-nba|url-status=live}}</ref> Starting with the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], coinciding with the start of a new [[NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement|collective bargaining agreement]] (CBA) between the NBA and [[National Basketball Players Association|its players' union]], the NBA adopted the WNBA's "positionless" format for All-NBA team composition—which the NBA had originally used before adopting a positional model in 1955–56.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10070887-report-all-nba-honors-to-be-positionless-in-new-cba-must-play-at-least-65-games |title=Report: All-NBA Honors to Be Positionless in New CBA; Must Play at Least 65 Games |first=Paul |last=Kasabian |website=Bleacher Report |date=April 1, 2023 |access-date=June 28, 2023 |archive-date=July 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705065907/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10070887-report-all-nba-honors-to-be-positionless-in-new-cba-must-play-at-least-65-games |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement – Key Deal Points|date=June 28, 2023|publisher=NBA|url=https://ak-static.cms.nba.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2023/06/2023-CBA-Summary.pdf|access-date=July 3, 2023|archive-date=June 28, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628202434/https://ak-static.cms.nba.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2023/06/2023-CBA-Summary.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> NBA players receive five points for a first team vote, three points for a second team vote, and one point for a third team vote. Starting in 2023–24, the five highest point totals regardless of position make up the first team, with the second and third teams following. During the positional era, the players with the highest point totals at each position made the first team, with the next highest making the second team and so forth.<ref name=nba_05262016/>  On one occasion, six players were placed on a team, when [[Bob Davies]] and [[Dolph Schayes]] tied for the first team in [[1951–52 NBA season|1952]]; the second team remained at five.<ref name="all-nba_b"/>

As part of effort to reduce [[Load management (sports)|load management]] for top stars in the league, the 2023–24 season introduced an eligibility threshold of 65 games played (out of the normal 82-game schedule) for most major regular-season playing awards and honors, including the All-NBA Team. To receive credit for a game for purposes of award eligibility, a player must have been credited with at least 20 minutes played. However, two "near misses", in which the player appeared for 15 to 19 minutes, can be included in the 65-game count. Protections also exist for players who suffer season-ending injuries, who are eligible with 62 credited games, and those affected by what the CBA calls "bad faith circumstances".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/more-details-emerge-on-new-nba-cba-including-details-on-65-game-threshold-for-awards |title=More details emerge on new NBA CBA, including details on 65-game threshold for awards |first=Kurt |last=Helin |work=NBC Sports |date=April 18, 2023 |access-date=June 28, 2023 |archive-date=June 28, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628202158/https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/more-details-emerge-on-new-nba-cba-including-details-on-65-game-threshold-for-awards |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://imgix.cosmicjs.com/25da5eb0-15eb-11ee-b5b3-fbd321202bdf-Final-2023-NBA-Collective-Bargaining-Agreement-6-28-23.pdf |title=Article XXIX, Section 6: Games Played Requirement for Certain League Honors |work=NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement |publisher=National Basketball Players Association |pages=432–38 |date=July 2023 |access-date=September 13, 2023 |archive-date=September 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230916202133/https://imgix.cosmicjs.com/25da5eb0-15eb-11ee-b5b3-fbd321202bdf-Final-2023-NBA-Collective-Bargaining-Agreement-6-28-23.pdf |url-status=live }} The games played requirement specifically applies to the MVP, Defensive Player of the Year, and Most Improved Player awards, as well as the All-NBA and All-Defensive Teams.</ref>

During the era of position-based team composition, voters were instructed to "vote for the player at the position he plays regularly",<ref name=larsen_07272020>{{cite news|first=Andy|last=Larsen|title=My NBA Awards ballot, Part 2: All-NBA, All-Defense, All-Rookie|date=July 27, 2020|newspaper=The Salt Lake Tribune|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2020/07/27/andy-larsen-my-nba-awards/|access-date=September 24, 2020|archive-date=September 23, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923210032/https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2020/07/27/andy-larsen-my-nba-awards/|url-status=live}}</ref> and some used the flexibility to designate a player at a position which was not their primary role.<ref name=larsen_07272020/><ref>{{cite news|first=Dan|last=Devine|title=Who Deserves All-NBA, All-Defensive, and All-Rookie Team Honors?|date=July 29, 2020|work=The Ringer|url=https://www.theringer.com/nba/2020/7/29/21346212/all-nba-defensive-rookie-teams-2020|access-date=September 24, 2020|archive-date=August 27, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200827231027/https://www.theringer.com/nba/2020/7/29/21346212/all-nba-defensive-rookie-teams-2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Nate|last=Scott|title=The All-NBA voting system is insane, but the league finally is addressing big issues|date=August 4, 2017|website=FoxSports.com|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/gallery/the-all-nba-voting-system-is-insane-but-the-league-finally-is-addressing-big-issues-040417|access-date=September 24, 2020|archive-date=September 25, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925035829/https://www.foxsports.com/nba/gallery/the-all-nba-voting-system-is-insane-but-the-league-finally-is-addressing-big-issues-040417|url-status=live}}</ref> A player who received votes at multiple positions was classified at the position in which they received the most votes.<ref name=nba_05262016/> This occasionally caused a player to be slotted to a lower team or miss an All-NBA selection altogether. For example, [[Draymond Green]] received votes at forward and center in [[2015–16 NBA season|2016]], but he was placed on the second team as a forward although he had more total points than the first-team center, [[DeAndre Jordan]].<ref name=nba_05262016/><ref>{{cite news|first=James|last=Herbert|title=Technicality robs Draymond Green of first-team All-NBA selection|date=May 26, 2016|website=CBSSports.com|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/technicality-robs-draymond-green-of-first-team-all-nba-selection/|access-date=September 21, 2020|archive-date=October 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021024936/https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/technicality-robs-draymond-green-of-first-team-all-nba-selection/|url-status=live}}</ref> In [[2019–20 NBA season|2020]], [[Khris Middleton]] garnered votes at both forward and guard, yet he was not on the third team despite having more points overall than [[Ben Simmons]] and [[Russell Westbrook]], who were selected at guard.<ref>{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Velazquez|title=Giannis unanimously selected as first-team all-NBA; Khris Middleton snubbed|date=September 16, 2020|newspaper=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2020/09/16/giannis-unanimously-selected-first-team-all-nba-middleton-snubbed/5817002002/|access-date=September 21, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|title=Giannis Antetokounmpo, LeBron James unanimously selected to 2019-20 All-NBA First Team|date=September 16, 2020|publisher=NBA|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/09/16/nba-2019-20-all-nba-teams-official-release|access-date=September 21, 2020|archive-date=September 18, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918173229/https://www.nba.com/article/2020/09/16/nba-2019-20-all-nba-teams-official-release|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[LeBron James]] has the most All-NBA selections with twenty-one. [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]], [[Kobe Bryant]], and [[Tim Duncan]] previously shared the record with fifteen.<ref name=botemps_09162020>{{cite news|first=Tim|last=Bontemps|title=Los Angeles Lakers' LeBron James sets record with 16th selection to All-NBA team|date=September 16, 2020|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29899984/los-angeles-lakers-lebron-james-sets-record-16th-selection-all-nba-team|access-date=September 17, 2020|archive-date=October 15, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211015221754/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29899984/los-angeles-lakers-lebron-james-sets-record-16th-selection-all-nba-team|url-status=live}}</ref> James also has the most All-NBA First Team honors with thirteen and is the only player to have done so as a member of three different teams,<ref name=botemps_09162020/> while Bryant and [[Karl Malone]] are tied for second-most with eleven.<ref name="all-nba_c">{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/all_league_by_player.html|title=All-League Selections by Player|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=August 7, 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080630080705/http://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/all_league_by_player.html| archive-date= June 30, 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref> Malone and James each share a record eleven consecutive first-team selections.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jai|last=Bednall|title=Millions gained and lost as All-NBA Teams announced|date=May 24, 2019|website=news.com.au|url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/american-sports/nba/millions-gained-and-lost-as-allnba-teams-announced/news-story/97dde85a236f79d63771591292905b13|access-date=September 17, 2020|archive-date=August 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803152915/https://www.news.com.au/sport/american-sports/nba/millions-gained-and-lost-as-allnba-teams-announced/news-story/97dde85a236f79d63771591292905b13|url-status=live}}</ref> James is both the youngest and oldest player to earn All-NBA honors, with his first All-NBA selection coming at the age of 20, and his most recent coming at the age of 40.<ref>{{cite news|first=Vishwesha|last=Kumar|title=LeBron James Is The Oldest And Youngest Player To Make An All-NBA Team|date=May 23, 2024|website=FadeawayWorld.net|url=https://fadeawayworld.net/lebron-james-oldest-youngest-player-make-all-nba-team|access-date=May 25, 2026}}</ref> [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] became the first [[List of NBA players born outside the United States|international player]] to be named All-NBA in 1985–86.<ref>{{cite web|first=Shaun|last=Powell|title=NBA vs. the World: A global game that would prove the game's might|date=February 17, 2023|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-vs-world-players-feature-all-star-2023|access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>  Since 2019, at least two international players have been named each season to the All-NBA First Team,<ref>{{cite news|first=Kyle|last=Irving|title=Joel Embiid MVP, All-International NBA Teams proof that the world has caught up with United States|date=May 3, 2023|work=Sporting News|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/joel-embiid-mvp-international-nba-world-united-states/dqr7wzpkc5wjhaajlqgee7io|access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref> including four players for the first time in 2023.<ref>{{cite news|title=All-NBA will be more like an All-World team this season, once again|date=April 9, 2024|work=TSN|agency=The Canadian Press|url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/all-nba-will-be-more-like-an-all-world-team-this-season-once-again-1.2101454|access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=NBA rumors: Four international players named in All-NBA First Team for the first time ever|date=May 11, 2023|work=HoopsHype|url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/four-international-players-named-in-all-nba-first-team-for-the-first-time-ever/|access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>

===1946–47 to 1954–55===
[[File:Bob Cousy NYWTS.jpg|thumb|right|upright|[[Bob Cousy]] was selected to the All-NBA team 12 times.|alt=A basketball player chases after a basketball across the court. He stands in front of two other players with jerseys with the words "NEW YORK"]]
[[File:Dolph Schayes.jpeg|thumb|right|upright|[[Dolph Schayes]] made an All-NBA Team every season of the 1950s.]]

From the [[1946–47 BAA season|1946–47 season]] to [[1954–55 NBA season|1954–55 season]], the All-NBA Team was composed of two teams, each with five roster spots, except when there were ties. During this period, players were selected without regard to position.

===1955–56 to 1987–88===
[[File:Bob Pettit 1957.jpeg|thumb|right|upright|[[Bob Pettit]] made 10 straight All-NBA First Teams from [[1954–55 NBA season|1955]] to [[1963–64 NBA season|1964]].]]
[[File:Jerry West (1959).jpg|thumb|right|upright|[[Jerry West]] made 12 All-NBA Teams - the seventh-most in NBA history.]]
[[File:Wilt Chamberlain Bill Russell (lighting fixed).jpg|alt=A basketball player, wearing a light-colored jersey with the number "13", is holding a basketball in front of another basketball player who is wearing a dark-colored jersey with the number "6".|thumb|upright|[[Bill Russell]] (left) has been selected to the All-NBA team 11 times.  [[Wilt Chamberlain]] (center) has been selected to the All-NBA team 10 times.]]
[[File:Kareem-Abdul-Jabbar Lipofsky (HQ).jpg|alt=A bald black person, wearing a gray suit and a tie, looks to the left.|thumb|upright|[[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] has been selected to the All-NBA team 15 times.]]
[[File:December 1983 One on One Dr J vs Larry Bird advertisement by Electronic Arts (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|right|[[Julius Erving]] (left) made 7 All-NBA teams, and [[Larry Bird]] (right) made 10 All-NBA teams.]]
[[File:Jordan by Lipofsky 16577 (high quality).jpg|alt=A smiling bald black man wearing a silver earring and herringbone jacket|thumb|upright|[[Michael Jordan]] has been selected to the All-NBA team 11 times.]]
[[File:Kobe Bryant Drives2.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Kobe Bryant]] has been selected to the All-NBA team 15 times.|alt=A black player near the basket with mouth open and right arm raised with ball in hand, preparing for a dunk.]]
From the [[1955–56 NBA season|1955–56 season]] to [[1987–88 NBA season|1987–88 season]], the All-NBA Team was composed of two teams, each with five roster spots, except when there were ties. During this time, players were selected with regard to position.

===1988–89 to 2022–23===
From the [[1988–89 NBA season|1988–89 season]] through the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23 season]], the All-NBA Team was composed of three teams, each with five roster spots, except when there were ties. Players were selected with regard to position.

===2023–24 to present===
Starting with the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], the All-NBA Team consists of three teams selected without regard to position, each with five roster spots, except when there are ties. Players will be listed in order of points received in voting; those tied on points will be listed in alphabetic order by family name.
